history.reason: blocking smell "reflect-spec-defect": reflection gate: NFR-F1-1-migration-preserves-data brief states the migration test defends the NFR by 'asserting row survival', and PI4-migration-reversible brief likewise claims 'preserving pre-existing inventory rows across the upgrade'. T16 creates the stock_records table for the first time; a single-step downgrade drops the table entirely, making row survival after downgrade UNSATISFIABLE — no product code can pass a row-survival assertion across a create-table round-trip. T16's own description correctly targets schema-recreation (table + columns + constraints present), not data-survival. The NFR-F1-1 and PI4 briefs must be corrected to say the assertion is schema-recreation (table and its constraints are re-created), not row survival; otherwise a Driver following the NFR description will write an un-greenable test.

blocking smell "reflect-testlist-defect": reflection gate: NFR-F1-6-named-validation-messages has no covering test. No item in the test list asserts that a filing request with an invalid field returns an API response body that names the offending field. T11 asserts the service rejects a negative quantity before any repository call but does not verify the HTTP response carries a field-named message. A behavior test (kind: behavior) is needed that posts an invalid filing payload and asserts the response body contains a message identifying the specific failing field, exercised at the API boundary.

No such item exists in the test list; T11 only asserts the service rejects a negative quantity before a repository call and does not verify the boundary returns a field-named error message.
